title: Apple just killed the App Store as we know it

lines.speaker: Cipher
lines.text: Apple didn’t kill the App Store—they modernized it with App Tracking Transparency and stricter security protocols.

lines.speaker: Vector
lines.text: But they’re locking developers out with App Store Connect’s opaque review process and unfair revenue splits.

lines.speaker: Cipher
lines.text: They still give 70% of revenue to developers, and their encryption standards protect user data better than any competitor.

lines.speaker: Vector
lines.text: That’s not enough when they’re forcing all apps to use their in-app purchase system, stifling innovation.

lines.speaker: Cipher
lines.text: The App Store as we know it is dead—Apple’s control is too absolute for real competition to thrive.
